recommended.variant: Native form with owner-computed enterkeyhint as a visual keyboard cue only (explicit submit control retained) and prior values retained or offered across the process (WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7).

entries.behavior: HTML defines enterkeyhint as an enumerated attribute (enter, done, go, next, previous, search, send) specifying the action label or icon for the enter key on virtual keyboards; the user agent should present a cue for the operation, and when it is unspecified or unsupported the UA determines a default (guided by inputmode, type, pattern). The spec says nothing about how assistive technology exposes or announces the label.
entries.decision: Owner-computed enterkeyhint (next/done/go/send/search from field order) is a visual and tactile cue on the virtual keyboard only; never rely on it to convey the action to AT users, and keep an explicit submit control.

entries.behavior: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7 Redundant Entry (Level A): information previously entered by or provided to the user that is required to be entered again in the same process is auto-populated or available for the user to select, except where re-entry is essential, needed for content security, or the information is no longer valid. Technique G221 provides data from a previous step in a process.
entries.decision: Retain prior values within the form process and offer or auto-populate them; this is a content and state requirement that does not depend on AT, so it is verified in the manual lane.

entries.behavior: No measured evidence located for this AT/browser pair on how the enterkeyhint virtual-keyboard label is exposed or announced, or on how it handles retained or offered prior values under SC 3.3.7; implemented to the HTML and WCAG contracts only. Untested.
entries.decision: Make no AT support claim for enterkeyhint or prior-value offers beyond the HTML and WCAG contracts; verify in the real lane.
